The live application below is running completely client-side in your browser using serverless Shinylive (WebAssembly). It provides a streamlined Systems Ethology platform (sysetholApp()) with clean sidebar controls (sysetholInput), dynamic conditional panels (Steps per click when nsim = 1, Confidence Band when nsim > 1), sidebar Run Engine & Reset buttons, and modular tabs (sysetholOutput: Dist Plots time-series step plots, Substrate Plots, Envelope Plots, and Input Data via inputApp).

title: sysetholApp (Systems Ethology Platform)
text:
Programmatic Application Usage
Launch the Systems Ethology Platform natively in R using exported package functions:
library(ewing)

# Launch interactive Systems Ethology platform app
sysetholApp()

# Or launch standalone Input Data Explorer
inputApp()
The app launcher script is located at inst/scripts/sysetholApp.R.

title: sysetholApp (Systems Ethology Platform)
text:
Platform Architecture & Features
The platform combines modular Shiny components exported in R/sysetholApp.R and R/inputApp.R:

Sidebar Setup & De-cluttering: Dynamic conditional panels display Steps per click when nsim = 1 and Total Simulation steps / Confidence Band Envelope when nsim > 1. Side panel Run Engine and Reset buttons keep the main interface focused and clean.
Dist Plots: Visualizes population age-class distributions over simulation steps (\(t = 0, 50, 100...\)) using geom_step() step lines and geom_point().
Substrate Plots: Projects organism positions onto hexagonal substrate topology overlays with species filtering and Overlay (1 Map) vs Separate (Stacked Maps) view modes.
Envelope Plots: Computes multi-run simulation envelopes across nsim stochastic iterations (visible when nsim > 1).
Input Data (inputApp): Interactive table explorer (inputAppInput, inputAppOutput, inputAppServer) for underlying organism.features, future.host, future.parasite, substrate.host, substrate.parasite, substrate.substrate, host.parasite, temperature.base, and temperature.par datasets.

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
← Back to Demos Gallery
The hexmapApp() application provides an interactive interface for discovering USGS subwatersheds, isolating specific geographic features (such as island landmasses), and projecting spatial hexagonal substrate networks for quantitative population ethology simulations.

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
Interactive Application Usage
You can launch the interactive application natively in R:
library(ewing)

# Launch interactive Shiny app
hexmapApp()

[!NOTE] Live Deployment: The interactive application requires dynamic spatial intersection libraries (sf) and live USGS / OpenStreetMap API access. It is deployed live on Posit Connect (HexMap).

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
section: Workflow Example: Isle Royale Watershed Projection
text:
Workflow Example: Isle Royale Watershed Projection
Below is an example showing how get_watershed() retrieves the USGS HUC12 subwatershed boundary (041800000101), clips it to the Isle Royale landmass using OpenStreetMap nominatim geometry (when osmdata is available), and overlays a spatial hexagonal grid (add_watershed_hex_overlay).

library(ewing)
library(ggplot2)

# Check if osmdata is installed for feature boundary restriction
feat_name <- if (requireNamespace("osmdata", quietly = TRUE)) "Isle Royale" else NULL

# 1. Fetch HUC12 boundary (optionally restricted to Isle Royale island landmass)
huc_info <- get_watershed("041800000101", feature_name = feat_name)

# 2. Construct spatial hexagonal overlay mesh (diameter = 0.01 degrees)
hex_obj <- add_watershed_hex_overlay(huc_info, hex_diameter = 0.01)

# 3. Visualize using autoplot
ggplot2::autoplot(hex_obj)

title: hexmapApp (Hexagonal Watershed Explorer)
text:
Technical Features

Leaflet Spatial Discovery: Click any location on North America or search landmark strings to reverse-geocode coordinates into USGS HUC12 subwatershed IDs (get_huc_from_point).
Feature Isolation: Clip large HUC boundaries covering open water to target landmasses (e.g. Isle Royale) using osmdata::getbb().
Hexagonal Mesh Scaling: Parameterize cell extent diameter to scale spatial resolution dynamically.
